items.name: garbage-token-storm

Re-verified in this audit on native lean 4.33.1: exactly three clean parse errors — 1:0 "unexpected token '$'" with the giant expected-command-token list (stresses diagnostics rendering), 4:23 and 5:2 backslash errors. Targets the garbage-typing-storm class that historically killed the worker.

items.name: tc_instance_depth_charge
items.source:
import Mathlib

set_option maxHeartbeats 400000

-- Deep DecidableEq derivation: needs a raised instance-size budget.
set_option synthInstance.maxSize 512 in
example : DecidableEq (List (Option ((Nat × Int × Bool) ⊕ (Fin 7 × List (Option (Bool × Nat)))))) :=
  inferInstance

-- Instance stacking through iterated products.
example : CommRing ((ℤ × ℤ) × (ℤ × ℤ) × (ℤ × ℤ)) := inferInstance

-- Lexicographic order synthesis.
example : LinearOrder (Lex (Fin 5 × Lex (Fin 3 × Fin 2))) := inferInstance

-- Decidability of a bounded quantifier through Fintype search.
example : Decidable (∀ x : Fin 6, ∀ y : Fin 6, x + y = y + x) := inferInstance

-- Pi-type DecidableEq stack.
example : DecidableEq (Fin 3 → Fin 3 → Bool) := inferInstance
items.rationale: Typeclass-search-heavy but terminating: deep DecidableEq/CommRing/LinearOrder/Fintype instance derivations over nested product, sum, Lex, and Pi types. Re-verified in this audit on the shipped wasm64 runtime + umbrella snapshot (snapshot-probe --via-mem): clean success in 917 ms. The first example genuinely exceeds the default synthInstance.maxSize 128, so the in-source set_option is load-bearing; every search is structurally bounded — no unbounded-search risk.

items.name: rec_depth_overflow_clean
items.source:
import Mathlib.Tactic

-- Meta-level whnf recursion overflow during `decide` must surface as the
-- CLEAN "maximum recursion depth" error, never a stack-blown worker crash.
set_option maxRecDepth 512 in
example : (List.range 300).length = 300 := by decide

-- Lowered limit: the same clean failure at a small depth.
set_option maxRecDepth 64 in
example : (List.range 100).foldl (· + ·) 0 = 4950 := by decide
items.rationale: Regression test for the JS-stack-overflow-kills-worker bug class: recursion past maxRecDepth must die via Lean's own guard, not the wasm/JS stack. whnf evaluation of List.range under decide reliably trips the guard — List.range 300 trips the pinned 512, and range 100 foldl trips a lowered limit 64. Re-verified in this audit on native 4.33.1: exactly two clean 'maximum recursion depth has been reached' errors (message text confirmed in fork Init/Prelude.lean), instant, worker-safe.

Re-verified in this audit on native 4.33.1 (core-only body): 0.73 s native, ~2-3 s wasm — comfortably inside budget, strictly bounded case count.

items.name: simp_loop_breaker
items.source:
import Mathlib.Tactic

-- Permutative lemma set: looks loopy, terminates via ordered rewriting.
example (a b c : Nat) : a + b + c = c + b + a := by
  simp [Nat.add_comm, Nat.add_left_comm]

axiom P : Nat → Prop
axiom P_shift (n : Nat) : P n ↔ P (n + 1)

-- Genuinely looping rewrite; the recursion/heartbeat budget must stop it
-- CLEANLY (and the "possibly looping" lint should fire).
set_option maxHeartbeats 40000 in
example : P 0 := by
  simp only [P_shift]
items.rationale: Two sides of simp termination: a permutative AC lemma set that terminates via ordered rewriting (must not loop), then a genuinely divergent P n ↔ P (n+1) rewrite that Lean must stop cleanly. Re-verified in this audit on native 4.33.1: warning 'Possibly looping simp theorem: `P_shift`' (message confirmed in fork LoopProtection.lean — the loop check is force-run after a recursion-depth failure) plus error 'Tactic `simp` failed with a nested error: maximum recursion depth...', instant. The maxHeartbeats 40000 in-source bound is the backstop; worker must survive. Stale-diagnostics and frozen-elaborating-pill regression bait.

items.name: structure_eta_mutual
items.source:
import Mathlib.Tactic

structure Pt where
  x : Nat
  y : Nat

-- Structure eta in defeq checks.
example (p : Pt) : p = ⟨p.x, p.y⟩ := rfl
example (p : Nat × Nat) : p = (p.1, p.2) := rfl
example (f : Nat × Nat → Nat) : f = fun p => f (p.1, p.2) := rfl

structure Sig where
  n : Nat
  h : n = n

example (s : Sig) : s = ⟨s.n, s.h⟩ := rfl

mutual
  inductive TreeN : Type where
    | node : Nat → ForestN → TreeN
  inductive ForestN : Type where
    | nil : ForestN
    | cons : TreeN → ForestN → ForestN
end

mutual
  def treeSize : TreeN → Nat
    | .node _ f => 1 + forestSize f
  def forestSize : ForestN → Nat
    | .nil => 0
    | .cons t f => treeSize t + forestSize f
end

example : treeSize (.node 5 (.cons (.node 1 .nil) .nil)) = 2 := by
  norm_num [treeSize, forestSize]
items.rationale: Structure-eta defeq edge cases (record eta under rfl, Prod eta, function-plus-structure eta, a dependent-field record) plus mutual inductive types with mutual recursive functions over them, computed via equation lemmas. Exercises the kernel's eta-for-structures path and mutual brecOn compilation — env-extension-epoch panic bait. Re-verified in this audit on the shipped wasm64 runtime + umbrella snapshot: clean success in 2130 ms.

items.name: universe_poly_edges
items.source:
import Mathlib.Tactic

universe u v w

def myId : ∀ {α : Sort u}, α → α := fun a => a

example : myId (myId (myId 3)) = 3 := rfl

set_option linter.checkUnivs false in
def liftTwice (α : Type u) : Type (max (max u v) w) := ULift.{w} (ULift.{v} α)

example : liftTwice.{0, 0, 0} Nat = ULift.{0} (ULift.{0} Nat) := rfl

example (n : Nat) : (ULift.up.{7} n).down = n := rfl

def piSort (α : Sort u) (β : α → Sort v) : Sort (imax u v) := ∀ a, β a

def nestOpt : Nat → Type
  | 0 => PUnit
  | n + 1 => Option (nestOpt n)

example : nestOpt 3 = Option (Option (Option PUnit)) := rfl

example : (Sort 0) = Prop := rfl

def pp : PProd PUnit.{u} PUnit.{v} := ⟨⟨⟩, ⟨⟩⟩
items.rationale: Universe-polymorphism edges: Sort-polymorphic id self-application, explicit max/imax level expressions, ULift at concrete high levels (ULift.up.{7}), a Nat-indexed Type-valued recursion reduced by kernel defeq, Sort 0 = Prop, and cross-universe PProd. Audit confirmed linter.checkUnivs is a real registered core option (fork src/Lean/Linter/CheckUnivs.lean), so the in-source silencing is valid and load-bearing. Re-verified on native 4.33.1: clean success in 0.11 s.

items.name: tactic_misuse_gauntlet
items.source:
import Mathlib.Tactic

-- decide on an undecidable universal: clean synthesis failure.
example : ∀ n : Nat, n + 0 = n := by decide

-- decide on a false decidable proposition: clean refutation.
example : (2 : Nat) + 2 = 5 := by decide

-- exact? after the goal is already closed: instant clean misuse error.
example : True := by trivial; exact?

-- sorry: warning only, session must stay alive.
example : False := by sorry
items.rationale: Tactic-misuse gauntlet, each probe failing cleanly and instantly: decide without a Decidable instance ('failed to synthesize' — lowercase confirmed in fork SynthInstance.lean), decide refuting a false prop ('Tactic `decide` proved that the proposition ... is false'), exact? invoked with no goals ('No goals to be solved' — chosen because a real exact? library search over the full umbrella env measured 63 s, blowing the budget), and sorry (warning 'declaration uses `sorry`'). AUDIT FIX: removed the original fifth probe (#eval ([] : List Nat).head!) — its deliberate PANIC output directly contradicts panicFree:true, since the harness fails any panicFree item whose output matches /PANIC/ (compiler-battery.mjs:49, e2e.mjs panicsInConsole). Re-verified in this audit on the shipped wasm64 runtime: three errors + sorry warning, all four fragments present, 881 ms.

theorem after : 2 = 2 := by rfl

example : True := by

Re-verified in this audit on native 4.33.1: exactly two clean 'unsolved goals' errors (⊢ 1 = 1 at the `by` token and ⊢ True at EOF) while the sandwiched 'after' theorem succeeds. Regression bait for the frozen-'elaborating'-pill and stale-diagnostics bug classes: two errors, correct positions, worker alive.

items.name: nested_by_matryoshka
items.source:
import Mathlib.Tactic

example : (1 = 1) ∧ (2 = 2) := by
  constructor
  · exact (by rfl)
  · have h : 2 = 2 := by
      have t : True := by exact (by trivial)
      rfl
    exact h

def natFromTactics : Nat := by
  have n : Nat := by exact (by exact 5)
  exact n + (by exact 2 : Nat)

example : natFromTactics = 7 := rfl

example : ∀ n : Nat, n + 0 = n := fun n => by
  induction n with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ k ih => simp
items.rationale: Nested 'by' blocks four layers deep in both Prop and data positions: term-mode 'by' inside tactic blocks inside 'have's, a Nat DEFINED entirely by nested tactics then computed by rfl, and 'by' under a lambda binder with induction. Exercises tactic-block info-tree nesting and elaborator suspension/resumption. Re-verified in this audit on native 4.33.1: clean success with zero warnings in 0.11 s.

items.name: canary_speed_heavy
items.source:
import Mathlib

set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000

-- Speed canary: known-good heavy work, all terminating.
example (a b c : ℤ) : (a + b + c) ^ 10 = (c + a + b) ^ 10 := by ring

-- 4096 kernel-evaluated cases.
example : ∀ x : Fin 64, ∀ y : Fin 64, (x.val * y.val) % 64 < 64 := by decide

example : (3 : ℕ) ^ 60 = 42391158275216203514294433201 := by norm_num

example : (2 : ℤ) ^ 127 - 1 = 170141183460469231731687303715884105727 := by norm_num

example (x y : ℚ) (h1 : x + 2 * y = 4) (h2 : 3 * x - y = 5) : x = 2 := by linarith

example (a b : ℤ) : (a + b) ^ 9 = a ^ 9 + 9 * a ^ 8 * b + 36 * a ^ 7 * b ^ 2 + 84 * a ^ 6 * b ^ 3 + 126 * a ^ 5 * b ^ 4 + 126 * a ^ 4 * b ^ 5 + 84 * a ^ 3 * b ^ 6 + 36 * a ^ 2 * b ^ 7 + 9 * a * b ^ 8 + b ^ 9 := by ring

example (a b c d : ℚ) (h1 : a + b + c + d = 10) (h2 : a - b = 1) (h3 : b - c = 1)
    (h4 : c - d = 1) : a = 4 := by linarith
items.rationale: KNOWN-GOOD heavy speed canary. Re-verified in this audit on the shipped wasm64 runtime + umbrella snapshot (snapshot-probe --via-mem): clean success in 7497 ms — squarely in the 5-10 s target with ~2.5x headroom under the 20 s budget. Mix of degree-10 ring normalization, a 4096-case kernel decide, exact 2^127-1 and 3^60 numerals via norm_num, two linarith systems, and the full degree-9 binomial expansion via ring. Any regression in elaborator, typeclass, norm_num-extension, or kernel-eval speed moves this number.

import Mathlib.Algebra.Algebra.Basic

inductive Tree (α : Type) where
  | leaf : Tree α
  | node : Tree α → α → Tree α → Tree α

def Tree.size : Tree α → Nat
  | .leaf => 0  
  | .node l _ r => l.size + r.size + 1

def Tree.mirror : Tree α → Tree α
  | .leaf => .leaf
  | .node l x r => .node r.mirror x l.mirror

theorem Tree.mirror_size (t : Tree α) : t.mirror.size = t.size := by
  induction t with
  | leaf => rfl
  | node l x r ihl ihr => simp [mirror, size, ihl, ihr]; omega
